speaker: Doctor
text: I need to clarify the nature of your symptoms. Do your double vision and weakness affect only one side of your body, and do your eyes move horizontally or vertically? Also, have you noticed any trouble swallowing or breathing?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms are highly suggestive of a neuromuscular junction disorder, specifically Myasthenia Gravis. Have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids or difficulty speaking clearly? REQUEST TEST: Acetylcholine_receptor_antibodies

speaker: Doctor
text: That confirms the presence of Myasthenia Gravis antibodies. Given your specific complaint of difficulty climbing stairs and upper limb weakness, do you experience any fatigue or weakness when lifting your arms above your head, or is the leg weakness more prominent? I would also like to see the results of your recent imaging studies to rule out any thymic abnormalities. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_XRay

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of ptosis, diplopia that worsens with upward gaze, fatigable proximal muscle weakness, and positive acetylcholine receptor antibodies is diagnostic; a chest X-ray was requested to screen for associated thymoma.
